diagnostic_evidence.quote: which has negative divergence and yields an indefinite problem with a grid P\'{e}clet number of approximately $3\,000$

issues.failure_explanation: The left-hand form is B_{ω_j^*}(χ_jφ,χ_jψ). For interior-supported functions, B(u,v)-B(v,u) = -2∫uv div b. With u=χ_jφ and v=χ_jψ this is -2∫χ_j^2 φψ div b, which is not zero when div b≠0. Its symmetric part is ∫A∇u·∇v + ∫uv div b, which is not positive semidefinite if div b has negative part, as in the paper's own rotating-velocity example. Hence the eigenproblem is not, in general, a symmetric positive (semi-)definite generalized eigenproblem, and the claimed real non-negative spectrum and SVD-based spectral approximation argument do not follow.

failure_location.quote: Note that, despite being based on the non-symmetric convection-diffusion equations, the above eigenvalue problem consists of two symmetric positive (semi-)definite bilinear forms, yielding only real and non-negative eigenvalues.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified for the advertised non-div-free regime; at minimum, the eigenproblem claim and dependent spectral theory must be restricted to divergence-free (or otherwise symmetric/coercive) cases, or replaced by a valid non-symmetric eigenvalue problem with a new analysis.
issues.overall_effect: The spectral coarse-space construction and the continuous MS-GFEM error/decay estimates are unsupported for the advertised non-divergence-free convection-diffusion regime. The divergence-free/coercive special cases may survive, but the general conservative-form extension does not.
issues.title: Local eigenproblem is claimed to be symmetric positive (semi-)definite in general
issues.why_classification: The defect invalidates the central spectral construction for a regime explicitly used in the paper. A comparable result would require excluding the non-div-free case or introducing essentially new non-symmetric eigenvalue theory, so the loss is major.

issues.failure_explanation: The remark quantifies the constants in the eigenvalue decay theorem with a factor containing 1/||b||_L^2(Ω)^2. The velocity field is allowed to be zero, and the paper explicitly considers pure-diffusion cases with b≡0. In that case the displayed constant C_j is undefined, so the quantification is false as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a separate diffusion-only case or replace the denominator by a bounded quantity such as max{||b||_L^∞^2,1}, with the corresponding limiting constant.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit constants given in the remark are not valid in the diffusion-only case. The existence of constants in the decay theorem is not itself disproved, but the remark's claim of quantification fails.
issues.title: Explicit decay constant is undefined for zero velocity
issues.why_classification: This is a local ill-defined formula in a quantification remark; a short case split or bounded denominator restores the claim without changing the main theorem's content or rate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: which maps a function $w \in \Hone$ to the MS-GFEM solution

issues.failure_explanation: The available MS-GFEM contraction estimate applies to the homogeneous/affine Dirichlet solution space: w must be the kind of function for which G w is the MS-GFEM approximation of w itself. For arbitrary w∈H^1 with nonzero Dirichlet trace, w is not the exact solution of the MS-GFEM problem with right-hand side B(w,·) under the same boundary lift, so the estimate ||w-Gw||_a ≤ vartheta||w||_a is not established. The proof also states a local-norm inequality over ω_j instead of the global a-norm needed for the contraction. Thus the stated any-H^1 initial-guess convergence is stronger than what the argument supports.

failure_location.quote: converges for any initial guess $\fwp^{(0)} \in \Hone$ strictly monotonically:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the theorem to initial guesses in u^e+H^1_D (or H^1_D for the homogeneous formulation) and correct the proof to use the global a-norm inequality ||(I-G)v||_{a,Ω} ≤ vartheta||v||_{a,Ω}.
issues.overall_effect: The continuous iterative MS-GFEM theorem overstates its admissible initial data. The contraction with rate vartheta is supported only for initial guesses in the natural affine space u^e+H^1_D (or H^1_D for the homogeneous problem), not for all H^1.
issues.title: Iteration theorem claims convergence for arbitrary H^1 initial guesses
issues.why_classification: The repair is a standard boundary-space restriction and a norm correction. It leaves the convergence rate, the continuous divergence-free setting, and the practical preconditioner scope essentially intact.

issues.failure_explanation: Let P_F=Σ_j R_j^T χ_j B_j^{-1}R_j and P_S=R_S^T B_S^{-1}R_S. The two-step iteration applies the coarse operator to the updated residual f-Bv^{k+1/2}=r-BP_F r, so the effective preconditioner is P_F + P_S(I-BP_F). The defined matrix, however, is P_F + P_S(I-P_F), missing the factor B on the fine-level correction in the coarse residual. Therefore the single-line preconditioned iteration and the described restricted additive Schwarz plus coarse correction do not implement the same operator.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the preconditioner definition to P_F + P_S(I - B P_F), or equivalently rewrite the single-line iteration to match the two-step residual update.
issues.overall_effect: The formally defined two-level hybrid RAS preconditioner has the wrong input-output contract. Any discrete interpretation or guarantee tied to the displayed matrix M B is inconsistent with the two-step algorithm actually described and presumably used numerically.
issues.title: Preconditioner matrix does not match the described two-step RAS iteration
issues.why_classification: The intended method is clear from the two-step equations, and the fix is a local formula correction. It does not require new proof architecture and does not change the advertised continuous theory or numerical algorithm if the split iteration is used.
